advice: Experiment: test 64×32 output macroblocks in the 512 assembly. Keep the current 32×32 FMOPA kernel and K loop. For each 64-row band, compute two adjacent 32-row C tiles for one 32-column B panel before advancing to the next B panel; retain the existing row-major-to-column-major operand mapping and cover all tiles once. Hypothesis: a smaller output macroblock may reduce scratch or B-panel working-set pressure. The supplied cache sizes alone do not show that cache traffic limits performance. Compare this distinct traversal against the incumbent with fresh paired controls under the fixed benchmark and promotion rules.
risks: Changing tile order and block dimensions can break panel addressing or omit/repeat C tiles. The smaller panel may add loop overhead or worsen locality. Preserve the ABI, FP32 operation, streaming transitions, per-call allocation rules, fallback, and BSD notice. Check tolerance at n=512 and general sizes, including odd tails and n<=0. Treat the hypothesis as unverified until repeated paired measurements clear the existing noise rules; do not attribute a joint result to this experiment alone.
